FIGURE 8-5  Movement of drugs after GI absorption. All drugs absorbed from sites 
along the GI tract—stomach, small intestine, and large intestine (but not the oral mucosa 
or distal rectum)—must go through the liver, via the portal vein, on their way to the heart 
and then the general circulation. For some drugs, passage is uneventful. Others undergo 
extensive hepatic metabolism. Still others undergo enterohepatic recirculation, 
a repeating cycle in which a drug moves from the liver into the duodenum (via the bile duct) 
and then back to the liver (via the portal blood). As discussed in the text under Enterohe-
patic Recirculation, the process is limited to drugs that have first undergone hepatic gluc-
uronidation. (From Lehne et al: Pharmacology of nursing care, ed 8, St Louis, 2012, Elsevier.)
